answer: Submissions that land within 142 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The pearl detector writes to signal, and karst shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 87 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 8 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
